findings.description: The reports bucket does not define server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) may be stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket, leaving it exposed to accidental public ACLs or bucket policies granting anonymous read/write.
The bucket has no logging block, so read/write access to the stored vendor data cannot be audited or attributed during an incident investigation.

Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irreversibly by an attacker (or ransomware) with write access, and force_destroy = true compounds the risk of unrecoverable data destruction.
The ledger export bucket holds financial data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data at rest is not protected with a managed KMS key.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, leaving no audit trail of access to exported ledger data.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, allowing silent overwrite or permanent deletion of financial export objects.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could expose ledger data publicly without an account-level backstop.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model data is stored unencrypted by configuration.
No public access block is attached, leaving the bucket dependent solely on the private ACL to prevent anonymous exposure.
The runbooks bucket, which typically stores operational procedures and sometimes embedded secrets or endpoints, has no server-side encryption configuration.
No logging block is defined, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block for this bucket, so public ACLs or policies are not categorically blocked.

The audit log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL, which grants the S3 log delivery group write and read-ACP permissions, and no public access block is configured to prevent further public grants on this sensitive audit data.

The audit trail bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no MFA delete or object lock, so log evidence can be destroyed wholesale by anyone able to run terraform destroy or delete the bucket, undermining the integrity of the audit record.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing PII/business-sensitive data) is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that itself has no default encryption, so the object is stored unencrypted.
